prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” health insurance broker for everyone in Kansas City — the right broker depends on what type of coverage you need (individual/ACA, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid, short‑term, self‑employed, etc.), whether you want an independent agent who shops multiple carriers, and how much hand‑holding you want during and after enrollment.

How to find the best broker for you
- Decide what kind of plan you need (ACA marketplace, employer/small‑group, Medicare/Advantage/Part D, short‑term, ACA off‑exchange, etc.). Different brokers specialize in different products.  
- Prefer independent/broker (not captive) if you want comparisons across multiple insurers. Ask whether they represent one carrier exclusively.  
- Verify licensing: check the Kansas Insurance Department to confirm the agent’s license and any disciplinary history. Ask for their NPN (producer) number.  
- Check reviews and references: Google/Yelp/BBB, LinkedIn, or ask the broker for recent client references in the Kansas City area.  
- Ask about fees/commissions: marketplace plans are typically free to you; other plans might involve broker commissions or fees—get this in writing.  
- Confirm ongoing service: will they help after enrollment (claims issues, mid‑year changes, renewals)? How will they communicate?  
- Ask these specific questions: how many clients like you do you serve? Which carriers do you work with locally? Do you do enrollment paperwork for me? How are you paid? Can I see client references?

Places to look right now
- Kansas Insurance Department website to verify licenses and file complaints.  
- HealthCare.gov (or your state’s exchange) for ACA marketplace plans and in‑person assister directories.  
- Medicare State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) for unbiased Medicare counseling.  
- Local independent agencies: search “independent health insurance agent Kansas City” and read reviews, or check NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) member directory for local advisors.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow suggestions if you tell me: your ZIP code, what kind of plan (ACA individual, Medicare, small business, etc.), and any preferences (independent agent, language, weekend hours).  
- Pull up a short list of well‑rated local brokers or agencies and their contact details.

Tell me what type of coverage you need and your ZIP code and I’ll find a few vetted options for Kansas City.
